fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Detached Structure; Detached Structure; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Vehicle Parking Area; Equipment Storage Area; Open Terrain
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Multiple Structures; Limited Rear Access; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the main driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions of approach.
• Mark each detached structure with a visible identifier so responders can communicate locations clearly during an incident.
• Keep all access drive surfaces clear of parked equipment and vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the rear of the property.
• Identify and mark any secondary access points so responding crews can quickly determine available entry routes.
• Keep gates serving the rear of the property unlocked or equipped with a rapid-release mechanism for emergency access.
• Clear a path wide enough for a responder on foot to move between each detached structure without obstruction.
• Designate and mark a flat, open staging area near the main access drive where emergency vehicles can park without blocking the drive.
• Keep the equipment storage area organized so that stored equipment does not block movement between structures or toward the open terrain.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Scattered Trees; Multiple Access Routes; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Wood Piles; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Move wood piles away from the house and any other structures, keeping them stored at a distance where flames could not reach the walls or roof.
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the house to increase the open space between the plants and the structure.
• Remove dead or dry material from scattered shrubs near any outbuildings or fenced areas.
• Keep the area directly around wood pile storage clear of dry leaves, twigs, and loose plant debris.
• Thin scattered trees near the house so their branches do not touch or hang over the roof or walls.
• Maintain open spacing between individual shrubs so fire cannot move easily from one plant to the next toward the structure.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
